core_obligations: Reduce to X reduced: replace X by its reduction, so that the generic points x_1, ..., x_n of the finitely many irreducible components are the only points that matter and the local rings K_i = O_{X,x_i} are fields, finitely generated over k because X is locally of finite type (proof lines 646-659).

Transfer the generic points through the base change: for every purely inseparable algebraic extension k'/k the morphism (X_{k'})_{red} -> X is a homeomorphism, so the points x'_i over the x_i are the generic points of the components of (X_{k'})_{red}, and their local rings are the fields (K_i tensor_k k')_{red} (proof lines 651-661).

Choose one extension for all components and conclude: by the algebra lemma there is a single finite purely inseparable k'/k making every (K_i tensor_k k')_{red} separable over k', hence geometrically reduced; the generic-point criterion then gives that (X_{k'})_{red} is geometrically reduced over k' (proof lines 661-670).
proof_roadmap: Replace X by its reduction and let x_1, ..., x_n be the generic points of its irreducible components (proof lines 646-650).
Use the homeomorphism (X_{k'})_{red} -> X to locate the generic points of the base change and identify their local rings as (K_i tensor_k k')_{red} (proof lines 651-661).
Apply the algebra lemma to find one finite purely inseparable k'/k making all these fields separable, then invoke the generic-point criterion for geometric reducedness (proof lines 661-670).
difficulty_reason: The lemma produces, for a scheme X locally of finite type over k with finitely many irreducible components, a single finite purely inseparable extension k'/k such that the reduction of X_{k'} is geometrically reduced over k' (statement lines 638-642). Three separate inputs are chained: the reduction lets one work with the generic points x_1, ..., x_n and their residue fields K_i; the purely inseparable base change is a homeomorphism, so the local rings of (X_{k'})_{red} at the points over the x_i are exactly the fields (K_i tensor_k k')_{red}; and one algebra lemma produces a single extension making all of them separable at once, after which the generic-point criterion closes the argument (proof lines 646-670). What is not routine is that one extension suffices for all components simultaneously. The claim is H2.
